bug_semantics: With escapeParameter/escapeParameterHtml enabled, Vue I18n escaped only interpolation values before inserting them into a translation template. When a trusted translation contains an HTML attribute and the translated result is rendered as HTML, an attacker-controlled parameter can still participate in an executable attribute context (including onerror or javascript: URL contexts); the option therefore did not provide the advertised DOM-XSS protection for the completed HTML string.
flaw_origin: PR #139 member 69489802dea27889ce323a8dd528a8d9da4aa0db first wrote the escapeParameter feature by applying escapeHtml only to list/named values before message interpolation and returning the completed translated string without sanitizing HTML attribute contexts. GitHub squash-merge 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef landed the identical tree on master. That incomplete security design is the vulnerable mechanism later corrected by sanitizing the final translated HTML.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object 69489802dea27889ce323a8dd528a8d9da4aa0db names author kazuya kawaguchi <kawakazu80@gmail.com> and committer kazuya kawaguchi <kawakazu80@gmail.com>; its message is 'feat: escap html parameter options' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other AI-attribution trailer/marker. GitHub squash-merge 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef of PR #139 has the same tree and also has no AI trailer.
evidence: Assigned bundle identifies GHSA-x8qp-wqqm-57ph / CVE-2025-53892, affected vue-i18n and @intlify packages, vulnerable ranges >=9.0.0 <9.14.5, >=10.0.0 <10.0.8, and >=11.0.0 <11.1.10, and first patched versions 9.14.5, 10.0.8, and 11.1.10.

CVE.org API record CVE-2025-53892 is PUBLISHED, names the same escapeParameterHtml DOM-XSS through tag attributes, confirms the vendor repository advisory, and references PRs #2229/#2230, commits 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099, and releases v9.14.5, v10.0.8, and v11.1.10.

git show 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef -- src/core/translate.ts src/utils.ts shows the first addition of escapeParameter, escapeParams(options), and escapeHtml; escapeParams transforms only list/named interpolation values before resolveMessageFormat, while translate returns the completed message without final-context sanitization.

git log -S'escapeParams(options)' -- src/core/translate.ts identifies 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef (2020-10-07, 'feat: escap html parameter options (#139)') as the first writer; later commits 22d57666e60e84a6c277cb24ac3c08f4e100d390 and 9ed153596c714f8542c1f8886b7034f361ab73bb are package-structure moves and are not BICs.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 gives immediate parent 34a31a83f6a712327774db2a7badda9866926c1a; git grep for escapeParameterHtml, escapeParameter, and escapeParams in that parent tree returns no match, directly proving parent absence.

git show -s --format=fuller plus the raw BIC message shows human author kazuya kawaguchi, GitHub committer, and no AI/co-author/generated trailer; no reconstructable PR-member ref for #139 exists in the validated local full-history clone, so 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef is the smallest surviving public first-write object.
merge-base ancestry checks show the BIC is contained in v9.0.0 and in affected-boundary tags v9.14.4, v10.0.7, and v11.1.9.

The branch-equivalent direct fixes 4aad98ee8c0e3de93c2b7de99fc5c745623cb1c4 (v11), 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e (v10), and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099 (v9) add sanitizeTranslatedHtml to the completed translation result and neutralize event-handler attributes and javascript: URLs; each immediate parent lacks sanitizeTranslatedHtml.

Tag containment and tree checks map 4aad98ee8c0e3de93c2b7de99fc5c745623cb1c4 to v11.1.10, 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e to v10.0.8, and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099 to v9.14.5; v11.1.9, v10.0.7, and v9.14.4 lack sanitizeTranslatedHtml, while each corresponding first-patched tag contains it.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and follows a closed source-to-sink lifecycle: attacker-controlled interpolation values flow through escapeParams/escapeHtml into a trusted translation's HTML attribute and then to an HTML-rendering sink, but the original option never sanitizes the resulting attribute context. The atomic first writer is 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef, not the later monorepo/package moves; its immediate parent lacks every feature entry point and helper. Release ancestry places that BIC before and inside all affected major lines. The three maintenance-line direct fixes add final-result sanitization exactly at v9.14.5, v10.0.8, and v11.1.10. Because AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object and that object has a human author with no AI marker or attribution trailer, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
